$comment: Dataset manifest for the tea classifier: what we have, where it came from,
how it is grouped, and how it will be split. Licences live in provenance.json;
class definitions live in taxonomy.json; measured numbers are reproduced by
The load-bearing field here is `groupBy`. Every dataset below ships augmented
copies of a smaller set of original photographs, and in both cases the
publisher's own split does not respect that. Splitting on images rather than
groups is the single mistake that would make every downstream number a lie.
raw_data_note: Images are NOT committed to this repository, not required by CC BY 4.0 and it would add ~1 GB. Fetch from the pinned DOIs in provenance.json; CS-D's archive is verified by SHA-256 below.

archive.structure: Nested RAR: outer archive contains six inner .rar files, one per class.

measured.claim_discrepancy: 671 fewer than the paper states; the entire shortfall is in Healthy (12,829 rather than 13,500). Every other class is exactly 13,500.
measured.dimensions: 256x256, uniform across a 300-image sample of every class

groupBy.rule: groupId = ((imageIndex - 1) mod 1500) + 1, where imageIndex is the integer in the filename, within each class folder.
groupBy.derivation: Not documented by the publisher, recovered empirically. For every class, the nearest neighbour of an image (by rotation/flip-invariant colour histogram) sits at index delta exactly 1500 for 96.5–96.8% of images, and at a multiple of 1500 for 99.5–99.9%. Mean nearest-neighbour similarity 0.9986–0.9988, i.e. siblings are near-identical. Reproduce with `verify_stride` in scripts/audit_tea_datasets.py.
groupBy.consequence: The nine images of a group are augmentations of one original photograph. They must never be separated across splits.

known_limitations: Only the augmented form is published. The 9,000 originals are not in the archive and cannot be recovered.

No estate, field, date, device or plant metadata of any kind. The paper describes seven Assam estates over seven months on three phone models, but none of that survives into the published files, so a geographic or temporal hold-out is impossible.
Images are pre-resized to 256x256 and median-filtered by the publisher, so the model cannot be trained at higher resolution and inherits their preprocessing.

datasets.format: Roboflow YOLOv8 export (object detection), converted to single-label classification

groupBy.rule: Roboflow names files <sourceStem>_jpg.rf.<hash>.jpg; the stem identifies the original photograph.
groupBy.consequence: Augmented copies share a stem and must stay together.

shipped_split_is_leaky.decision: DISCARD the shipped split entirely and re-split by source stem.

known_limitations: Roboflow's export log states augmentation created 2 versions of each source image via random horizontal and vertical flips, then split randomly, which is how siblings ended up straddling splits.
Images are of DETACHED leaves against varied backgrounds, closer to a lab protocol than a farmer photographing a bush.

Filenames fall into three distinct families (2,424 camera-timestamp, 2,336 generic image_N_N, ~330 UNADJUSTEDNONRAW_thumb), suggesting three different sub-collections merged into one dataset with different capture conditions.
79 images carry no bounding box at all and therefore have no usable label.

datasets.finding: The Mendeley record, the CC BY 4.0 grant this dataset's licence clearance rests on, contains no image files in ANY version. Versions 1, 2 and 3 are empty; version 4 contains a single 187 KB read_me.pdf and nothing else.
datasets.decision: DROPPED as the cross-dataset partner. The counts above are transcribed from the readme for the record and are NOT verified against pixels, because there are no pixels to verify.
datasets.note: A Kaggle mirror exists, but taking images from a mirror would break the provenance chain: the CC BY 4.0 grant we verified attaches to the Mendeley record, and a mirror's contents and licence would need independent verification. Not worth it when licence-clean alternatives exist.

datasets.role: cross_dataset_test_secondary (TEST ONLY - never training, never model selection)

archive.note: v1 and v2 are byte-identical (same sha256); the version bump changed metadata only.
archive.structure: Two parallel top-level sets the record does not mention: 'Tea Compressed Data' and 'Tea Original Data', each holding the SAME 2,008 images per class (301/302/436/321/332/316). The originals are the full-resolution source of the compressed set, 4,016 files in total.

measured.dimensions: Dominant 640x480 LANDSCAPE, not the 480x640 the record states. Both orientations present, plus 471x640/477x640/438x640 and one 4000x3000 in the compressed healthy folder.

exif.gps_present: 0 of 4,016 (0.0%) in BOTH the compressed and original sets
exif.date_discrepancy: EXIF is 16 months earlier and spans two days, not eight. EXIF is written by the camera at capture and is trusted over the record.
exif.sweep: EXHAUSTIVE - all 4,016 files in both sets, not a sample.

datasets.estate_split_finding: NO - confirmed by exhaustive sweep of all 4,016 files. Zero carry EXIF GPSInfo, while 100% carry some EXIF and 99.8% carry DateTimeOriginal. GPS was therefore never recorded, not stripped by the publisher's compression. Images are foldered by CLASS in both sets; there is no estate directory, manifest or filename token. The two named estates exist only in the record's prose.

device_class_confound.finding: Device is strongly confounded with class.
device_class_confound.impact: Three classes are effectively single-device, so a model could key on sensor noise, colour science or JPEG quantisation rather than the lesion. Also rules out device or capture date as a split axis, since either would remove whole classes from one side.
device_class_confound.decision: TEST ONLY. As a test set the confound makes the test harder, not dishonest. As training data it would teach the camera.

groupBy.rule: Consecutive IMG_#### camera shutter numbers form a burst of the same leaf. iOS 'IMG_E####' is the EDITED copy of 'IMG_####' and belongs to the same group.
groupBy.measured: 483 runs across 2,008 images, mean 4.2 images per run. 38 edited/original pairs within the same class.
groupBy.near_duplicates: Mean nearest-neighbour similarity 0.9706 (CS-D: 0.9988); 6.8% above 0.999. Genuinely diverse by comparison.

label_mapping.note: All six folder names already resolve through teaClassFromSourceLabel with NO taxonomy change required.

overlap_with_active_v1.value_added: red_spider_mite is NOT in the EWU overlap, so TLD-BD lifts cross-dataset coverage from 3 of 6 active classes to 4 of 6, using genuine in-field imagery rather than EWU's detached leaves.

datasets.classes_NOT_activated: grey_blight, algal_leaf_spot and looper stay inactive. None appears in CS-D, so none can be trained; presence in a test set is not a reason to activate a class.

datasets.rejected_because: Every leaf is photographed against a BLACK BACKGROUND. As a held-out set it would measure background shift rather than generalisation, and as training data it would teach the background. 7 GB for a domain we do not serve.
datasets.useful_finding: This team also ships 'Algal Leaf Spot' and 'Red Rust' as SEPARATE classes, independent corroboration for keeping them unmerged in the taxonomy.

blister_blight_availability.implication: The flagship Sri Lankan tea disease, and the one lib/grow/risk.ts is built around, exists in exactly one dataset. It cannot be cross-dataset validated by any source found. This is the single most important caveat attached to the model.

split.method: sha256(datasetId|className|groupId) → first 4 bytes as uint32 → mod 100 → <70 train, <85 val, else test
properties: Deterministic and machine-independent, no stored split file to lose or diverge.
Stable under growth: adding a class or more images never reshuffles what is already assigned.
Whole groups move together, so an augmented sibling can never straddle a boundary.
Keyed by dataset id too, so CS-D group 7 and EWU group 7 are unrelated.
split.cs_d_group_preview_note: Groups, not images. Close enough to 70/15/15 without forcing exact ratios, which would require a global sort and break the stability-under-growth property.
evaluation_plan: TIER 1 - Internal group-held-out test (CS-D). Whole source groups held out via the sha256 group hash. Reported per class. This is an IN-DISTRIBUTION number; it must never be presented as generalisation.
TIER 2 - Cross-dataset test (EWU), re-split by Roboflow source stem. Classes: healthy, brown_blight, helopeltis. Detached-leaf domain.
TIER 3 - Cross-dataset test (TLD-BD), test-only. Classes: healthy, helopeltis, red_spider_mite. Real in-field domain, two Bangladesh estates, different devices.
Tiers 2+3 together cover 4 of 6 active classes: healthy, brown_blight, helopeltis, red_spider_mite.

NO cross-dataset number exists for blister_blight or red_rust. Blister blight appears in no other dataset examined; red_rust appears only in TeaLeafDiseaseBD, which was rejected for its black studio background.
Model selection uses the CS-D validation split ONLY. Tiers 1-3 test sets are touched once, after training is frozen.
Report expected calibration error and a reliability diagram alongside accuracy, per class, never a single headline number.

final_composition.training: CS-D only. 6,270 source groups (~55,900 images) across 6 classes.
final_composition.test_tier2_cross_dataset: EWU, re-split by source stem, 3 overlapping classes.
final_composition.test_tier3_cross_dataset_field: TLD-BD, all 1,073 images in the 3 overlapping classes. Test only.
final_composition.rationale: CS-D is the only source containing blister blight, so it must carry training. EWU and TLD-BD are reserved entirely for measurement, which is the only way their numbers mean anything.
